newsitem.title: USA: UTC sets 2-for-1 stock split, boost Russian investment.
newsitem.headline: UTC sets 2-for-1 stock split, boost Russian investment.

text.p: United Technologies Corp. Monday announced a two-for-one stock split and said it planned to increase investments in Russia to $250 million from $125 million in the next few years.
United Technologies' subsidiaries Pratt and Whitney, Carrier, Hamilton Standard and Otis are already active in Russia.
"UTC's joint ventures in Russia already employ over 10,000 Russians, making UTC one of the largest joint venture employers outside the energy sector," the company said in a statement.
The company's board of directors were to meet in St. Petersburg, Russia, Monday, said a company official, who asked not to be identified. He did not give the details of the meeting's agenda.
Hartford, Conn.-based United Technologies provides high technology products and support services to the building systems, automotive, and aerospace industries.

A stock dividend will be distributed in December to shareholders of record as of Nov. 22. The board also doubled the outstanding authorisation for the repurchase of UTC common stock in keeping with the stock split.
United Technologies' stock rose 75 cents to $121 on the New York Stock Exchange at midday.
